findings.title: A failed setup USE now drops the new connection, but the pool's `current_keyspace` gets…
findings.claim: A failed setup USE now drops the new connection, but the pool's `current_keyspace` gets set before the keyspace is validated and is never rolled back. One bad `Session::use_keyspace` or `DROP KEYSPACE` call therefore stops the pool from ever refilling. Before this PR, the connection logged a warning and was still published.

findings.title: The PR balances total_connections at each explicit clear site but not when the…
findings.claim: The PR balances total_connections at each explicit clear site but not when the PoolRefiller itself is dropped, so the metric still leaks.

findings.title: Keyspace setup failures used to be logged at `warn
findings.claim: Keyspace setup failures used to be logged at `warn!` and are now logged only at `debug!`, while the consequence got more severe: the connection is discarded and the pool can report Broken. The format also switched from `{:?}` to `{}`, unlike the sibling arms.

findings.title: The new Display string does not match the sibling description of the same failure
findings.claim: The new Display string does not match the sibling description of the same failure. ExecutionError::UseKeyspaceError renders "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}", while the new ConnectionError variant renders "Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection: {0}". Inside ConnectionError, setup-request siblings (ConnectionSetupRequestError) are `transparent` and carry the request kind instead.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state awaits ready_connections
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state awaits ready_connections.next() with no timeout.

findings.title: The test `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` only asserts `need_filling()`
findings.claim: The test `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` only asserts `need_filling()`. It never drives `run()`, so it does not check the PR's claim that 'the pool schedules another refill'. It also builds the failure event with `keyspace_name: None`, which production never produces for keyspace failures.

findings.title: The new keyspace tests build PoolRefiller by hand instead of using the existing…
findings.claim: The new keyspace tests build PoolRefiller by hand instead of using the existing mock_pool_refiller helper, and skip setup_tracing.

findings.title: The same OPTIONS/STARTUP proxy rule construction is now copied in several new tests…
findings.claim: The same OPTIONS/STARTUP proxy rule construction is now copied in several new tests instead of reusing start_simulated_node.

findings.title: None of the four commits has a message body
findings.claim: None of the four commits has a message body. Nothing in the history explains why keyspace-setup failures now discard the connection when they used to keep it, or why the metric decrements were added.

findings.title: The two new keyspace tests never call `setup_tracing()`, which the repo requires of new…
findings.claim: The two new keyspace tests never call `setup_tracing()`, which the repo requires of new tests. The neighbouring new metrics tests do call it.

findings.title: The comment in the Ok branch still says a connection that needs a keyspace will 'travel…
findings.claim: The comment in the Ok branch still says a connection that needs a keyspace will 'travel through this logic again, to be finally put into the conns'. This commit makes that false whenever USE fails, because the connection is now discarded.

findings.title: The new `decrement_total_connections` helper is applied at three clear sites, but the…
findings.claim: The new `decrement_total_connections` helper is applied at three clear sites, but the shard-aware excess path at connection_pool.rs:1006 still drops an accepted, metric-counted connection without decrementing `total_connections`.

findings.title: The metric decrement is now done by hand at every place a connection vector is cleared…
findings.claim: The metric decrement is now done by hand at every place a connection vector is cleared or a connection dropped: the run loop, the excess limit, maybe_reshard, the Keyspace arm and remove_connection. The decrement-then-clear pair is copied at each site instead of living in one place.

findings.title: The new private enum `ConnectionSetupError { Connection, Keyspace }` duplicates the…
findings.claim: The new private enum `ConnectionSetupError { Connection, Keyspace }` duplicates the classification the same change adds to the public `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError`. Its name is also easy to confuse with the existing public `ConnectionSetupRequestError`.

findings.title: The new Keyspace-failure arm copies the `
findings.claim: The new Keyspace-failure arm copies the `!self.is_filling() && self.is_empty()` report condition from the Connection arm but not the explanatory comment, so the two copies of the condition can drift.

findings.title: The test `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` does not prove that a refill gets…
findings.claim: The test `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` does not prove that a refill gets triggered.

findings.title: The synthetic event in `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` cannot occur in production
findings.claim: The synthetic event in `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` cannot occur in production. It pairs a Keyspace error with `keyspace_name: None`, while start_setting_keyspace_for_connection always sets `Some(keyspace_name)`.

findings.title: The new tests copy fixtures instead of reusing helpers
findings.claim: The new tests copy fixtures instead of reusing helpers. Two tests construct `PoolRefiller::new(...)` by hand, duplicating `mock_pool_refiller`. `make_rules` and the resharding test re-implement the OPTIONS/STARTUP rules from `start_simulated_node`.

findings.title: The test forges a SET_KEYSPACE RESULT body as the undocumented byte literal…
findings.claim: The test forges a SET_KEYSPACE RESULT body as the undocumented byte literal `b"\0\0\0\x03\0\x08keyspace"`. The literal silently depends on the keyspace name 'keyspace' that is set separately.

findings.title: The `unrequested_connection_event` helper is gated on `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]`…
findings.claim: The `unrequested_connection_event` helper is gated on `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` although it has nothing to do with metrics. Every caller also has to call `metrics.inc_total_connections()` by hand first to mimic count_in_metrics.

findings.title: Proxy teardown is inconsistent across the new tests
findings.claim: Proxy teardown is inconsistent across the new tests. `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` calls `proxy.finish()` while the refiller still holds live connections and drops the refiller afterwards. It then has to whitelist DriverDisconnected. The sibling tests drop the refiller first and ignore the finish result with `let _ =`.

findings.title: The stated validation command does not enable the `metrics` feature, which is not a…
findings.claim: The stated validation command does not enable the `metrics` feature, which is not a default feature. All metric assertions in the keyspace tests are compiled out. The three metrics regression tests from commit 0d91aa54 are also excluded, both by cfg and by the test-name filter.

findings.title: Commit de164845 changes metric behavior with no tests
findings.claim: Commit de164845 changes metric behavior with no tests. The tests arrive only in the next commit, 0d91aa54.

findings.title: The keyspace check now runs before sharder learning (`maybe_reshard`), shard-aware port…
findings.claim: The keyspace check now runs before sharder learning (`maybe_reshard`), shard-aware port learning, and the advanced-shard-awareness mismatch check. Topology learning now waits for USE to finish, and a USE that fails or hangs means the node's new sharder and port are never learned from that connection.

findings.title: The PR body describes only the keyspace change
findings.claim: The PR body describes only the keyspace change. It omits the metric-balancing behavior change in de164845, its tests in 0d91aa54, and the test fix in 617139df.

findings.title: Commit 617139df is a fixup for the test added in 0d91aa54
findings.claim: Commit 617139df is a fixup for the test added in 0d91aa54. It replaces a `yield_now` busy-wait polling loop with a sleep. The original commit's test therefore needed a later fix instead of being squashed into it.

findings.title: The new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant adds a From<UseKeyspaceError>…
findings.claim: The new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant adds a From<UseKeyspaceError> impl and a new message format to a public non_exhaustive enum. The pool only ever stores it as the Broken pool error.

findings.title: A keyspace failure on a shard-aware attempt sets had_error_since_last_refill and has no…
findings.claim: A keyspace failure on a shard-aware attempt sets had_error_since_last_refill and has no fallback path. The test asserts only the error flag and does not cover requested_shard semantics.

findings.title: In maybe_reshard, the decrement for excess connections sits above `self
findings.claim: In maybe_reshard, the decrement for excess connections sits above `self.conns.clear()`, while `self.excess_connections.clear()` is several lines further down, so the metric accounting is separated from the clear it pays for.

findings.title: The keyspace-failure branch calls `self
findings.claim: The keyspace-failure branch calls `self.metrics.dec_total_connections()` directly, while the PR adds a `decrement_total_connections(count)` helper and remove_connection uses yet another inline call. That leaves three different decrement idioms in one file.

findings.title: The new tests copy the proxy OPTIONS/STARTUP rule fixtures from start_simulated_node and…
findings.claim: The new tests copy the proxy OPTIONS/STARTUP rule fixtures from start_simulated_node and hand-encode a SET_KEYSPACE RESULT body as a raw byte literal, so protocol and fixture rules now live in several places.

findings.title: Adding a public `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` variant contradicts the enum's doc,…
findings.claim: Adding a public `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError` variant contradicts the enum's doc, which says the error means the connection can no longer be used and should be dropped, and it widens the public API to carry this failure.

findings.title: Setup USE is now an explicit gate that both publishing and topology learning wait on,…
findings.claim: Setup USE is now an explicit gate that both publishing and topology learning wait on, and it still has no timeout. The TODO remains. By contrast, the pool's own use_keyspace bounds the same request with connect_timeout.

findings.title: The new public `#[from] UseKeyspaceError` conversion changes which ConnectionError…
findings.claim: The new public `#[from] UseKeyspaceError` conversion changes which ConnectionError variant callers see for a broken connection. If a connection breaks during setup USE, callers now get `ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError(RequestError(BrokenConnectionError))` instead of `ConnectionError::BrokenConnection`.

findings.title: The keyspace-failure branch does not compare the failed `evt
findings.claim: The keyspace-failure branch does not compare the failed `evt.keyspace_name` with `self.current_keyspace`. If the user switched keyspace while a setup USE was in flight, a failure for the old keyspace still sets the backoff flag and can publish a stale Broken error.

findings.title: All four commits are title-only, with no body explaining why
findings.claim: All four commits are title-only, with no body explaining why. This conflicts with the contribution rule. 7f48315d also bundles the error-propagation change with a reordering of the keyspace check ahead of resharding and port learning, and its message does not mention the reordering.
